Definition: Integration of company registration, business licensing, tax compliance, regulatory compliance data
Comments: E-procurement (e-GP) is referenced in the Digital Gabon Project as a target service for transformation. The Unique Participation File (FUP, January 2026) centralizes government participation data in projects. Business registration integration with the interoperability platform is planned but not yet implemented, as no entities are yet connected to the platform per World Bank ISR (June 2024).

Definition: Integration of CRVS data (births, deaths, marriages) into data exchange for real-time verification and service eligibility
Comments: The Digital Gabon Project includes digitalization of the civil registration (CR) system as a major component. An adequate legal and regulatory framework for digitalized civil registration is a project target (not yet achieved as of June 2024 per World Bank ISR, which records baseline and current values as 'No'). The target is 15 administrative departments with at least one digitally registered vital acts office by June 2026. Integration with the broader data exchange layer is not yet operational.

Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: Gabon launched the Electronic National Identity Card (CNIE) with a 14-digit NIP in June 2024, supplied by IN Groupe (France). A civil registry NIP issuance campaign began in Libreville in May 2024. However, the World Bank ISR (June 2024) records 0% of population 16+ with a NIP. CNIE is intended to serve as the authentication backbone for the future interoperability platform, but integration is not yet operational. The NIP system replaces an 11-year gap in ID card issuance.

Definition: Integration of health records, patient registration, immunization data, and health insurance into data exchange
Comments: The eGabon CI-SIS (Clinical Information System Interoperability Framework) was developed under the eGabon-SIS project (launched 2016). A Strategic Master Plan for the National Health Information System (SDSSIS, 2017) and an eHealth interoperability framework were developed, including use cases for patient admission, laboratory, imaging, health surveillance, and patient identifier (ISG). The project reached a pilot phase by 2021. The CNAM-GS (National Health Insurance and Social Security Fund) is a major data system. Full integration with the broader government data exchange layer is not confirmed.

Definition: Integration of passport issuance and immigration control data into the exchange platform
Comments: The CNIE electronic identity card is planned for use as a travel document within CEMAC countries (policy since 2008 for visa-free travel with biometric passport). An e-Visa system exists. The Digital Gabon Project includes legal identity modernization that will eventually support passport services. Full integration with the data exchange layer is under development.

Definition: Integration with national payment systems for government-to-person (G2P), government-to-business (G2B) transactions via data exchange
Comments: The MADIGIPAIE project (introduced January 2026) will facilitate electronic payments for public services. The SIGFIP Integrated Public Finance Management System was launched January 2026. CEMAC/GIMACPAY regional payment interoperability infrastructure exists. Gabon has the highest digital payments usage in the CEMAC region (World Bank DE4A diagnostic). A national platform for the payment and collection of public revenue is planned. Full integration with the government data exchange layer is not yet confirmed.

Comments: SIGFIP (Integrated Public Finance Management System) launched January 2026 to streamline government financial operations. Electronic invoicing systems are being implemented. Full G2G data exchange integration is under development.

Definition: Whether a detailed implementation roadmap with phases, milestones, and timelines exists for data exchange development
Comments: The Digital Gabon Project (2021-2026) provides a phased implementation roadmap with four defined components: (1) enabling environment for digital transformation ($20M), (2) modernizing legal ID systems ($24.5M), (3) digital transformation of public administration and services ($17M), and (4) citizen engagement and M&E ($7M). Closing period June 2026. The eGabon and Gabon Digital programs have a steering committee with performance indicators and monitoring.

Definition: Whether a formal strategy or policy document exists specifically for government data exchange and interoperability
Comments: Comprehensive strategy exists. Gabon's Strategic Plan for an Emerging Gabon (PSGE, 2009, targeting digital excellence by 2025), the Accelerated Transformation Plan (PAT, 2021-2023), the World Bank DE4A Digital Economy Diagnostic (2019/2021), and the Digital Gabon Project appraisal (2021) collectively provide a comprehensive framework for government data exchange and interoperability. The Digital Gabon Project explicitly targets a government-wide Common Interoperability Framework (CIF).

Definition: Current operational status of the data exchange system
Comments: A government-wide interoperability platform is under development as part of the World Bank-funded Digital Gabon Project ($68.5M, signed January 2024). The World Bank Implementation Status Report (June 2024) records 0 government entities actively exchanging data on the platform and the interoperability platform as not yet deployed. The 5th steering committee (February 2026) noted that 'foundations are in place but disbursement rates remain too low.' No operational data exchange system exists as of early 2026.

Definition: Extent to which the data exchange enables services accessible to all population groups including persons with disabilities, elderly, low literacy
Comments: The Digital Gabon Project targets inclusive access, specifically for vulnerable and marginalized groups. World Bank ISR (June 2024) tracks female NIP holders as a target (50% female target) and rural-to-overall NIP coverage ratio. UN EGDI 2024 score is 0.5741 (rank 121/193), placing Gabon in the High EGDI group. E-Participation index score is 0.1233 (2024 rank not top tier). Accessibility provisions are planned but not yet operational.

Definition: Extent to which provincial/state and local governments participate in the data exchange
Comments: An inter-ministerial committee under the Prime Minister's office was created February 2021 to coordinate digital public administration initiatives with ANINF (Agency for Digital Infrastructure and Networks of Gabon) as coordinator. Sub-national participation in data exchange is planned but the platform has not yet been launched. No evidence of regional or local government entities currently exchanging data on any platform.

Definition: Whether data exchange infrastructure and services reach rural and remote areas or concentrate in urban centers
Comments: Gabon has strong infrastructure: 94% of population covered by 3G/4G (ARCEP/GSMA 2020), 1.919 million Internet subscribers (June 2020), and a national fiber-optic backbone of 1,030 km. However, the World Bank Digital Gabon Project ISR explicitly targets a rural-to-overall NIP coverage ratio of 1.0 (baseline 0.0), acknowledging a rural-urban gap. The World Bank DE4A diagnostic notes persistent digital exclusion in rural areas.
